protocol: Agenda 24 Nov / 01 Dec: LoRA fine-tuning of Bolmo 1B in the all-in-one and step-by-step setups, for each low-resource language (ain, ddo, jje); hyperparameter tuning not now.
languages_note: Languages, dataset manifests, prompt files and few-shot settings are read from configs/zero_shot.json (one source for zero-shot, few-shot and LoRA). --lang is a key of its 'languages'.
strategies_note: Both are one call and use the zero-shot prompt files (zero_shot/prompts/all_in_one.txt, step_by_step.txt) with {language} filled in. Same answer format (Transliteration line + Gloss line); they differ only in the instructions. The old two-call two_stage LoRA setup is removed.

adapter.target_modules_note: Bolmo-1B = byte-level local encoder/decoder (xLSTM) around a 16-layer global transformer. LoRA goes on q_proj/v_proj of the 16 global layers only (32 modules); the regex excludes the boundary predictor's q_proj_layer and the xLSTM q/k/v. The runner fails if the match count is 0 and records the matched names.

training.max_seq_bytes_note: Bolmo is byte-level: <bos> + prompt + answer + <eos>. Longer train/dev examples are left out of training / validation loss and listed in run_meta.json (never truncated); a warning is printed above 1%. lora/check_data.py (26 Nov): 2048 leaves out 2 of 6726 Ainu and 2 of 3558 Tsez train rows (longest 2911 bytes), no Jejueo rows and no dev rows.
training.precision: bf16 on GPUs with compute capability >= 8 (A100, L4), else float32 (T4)
training.eval_every_epochs_note: The plan saves after each epoch; every 0.5 epoch is a superset (epochs 1, 2, 3 are among the six checkpoints) and is kept for all runs so they stay comparable.
training.resume_every_steps_note: Quick resume save (adapter + optimizer state, overwritten each time, not evaluated) so a Colab disconnect loses at most 20 optimizer steps.

runs_note: Agenda 24 Nov: hyperparameter tuning not now, so only 'baseline' (r16, alpha 32, lr 2e-4) is planned. r8 / r32 / lr1e-4 stay available (one factor at a time) for later.

generation.max_new_bytes_note: Same budget for both strategies (one call: transliteration line + gloss line). Longest gold answer (lora/check_data.py, 26 Nov): test Ainu 819, Tsez 677, Jejueo 454 bytes; dev Tsez 658 (9 dev rows > 512), so 1024 covers every dev/test answer. Training appends an end-of-sequence byte, so the model learns to stop; the budget only matters for outputs that do not stop.
